claims.claim: Ordered-bipartition criterion: a bipartite n-vertex tree with classes A={x1,...,xa} and B={y1,...,yb} has a bipartition-separated graceful labeling if and only if the two classes can be ordered so that the endpoint-rank sums i+j over edges xiyj are pairwise distinct.
claims.evidence: There are n−1 edges and every rank sum is in {2,...,n}; distinctness therefore makes the sums exactly that set. Given the orders, phi(x_i)=i and phi(y_j)=n+1−j use every label once and give difference n+1−(i+j), hence exactly 1,...,n−1. Conversely, complement if necessary so A is the lower class, order A by increasing labels and B by decreasing labels, and the same identity turns distinct graceful differences into distinct rank sums.
claims.search_method: Direct bijective algebraic proof in both directions.

claims.claim: For every caterpillar, the bipartition orders described in the final writeup give endpoint-rank sums 2,3,...,n in succession.
claims.evidence: The first leaf edge has rank sum 2. Within a leaf block, the leaf rank increases by one. From the last leaf edge to the following spine edge, the next spine vertex immediately follows that leaf block in the same class order. From a spine edge to the first leaf edge at the next spine vertex, that leaf immediately follows the preceding spine vertex in the other class order. Thus every successive listed edge raises the sum by one, including across empty blocks. With n−1 edges, the sequence ends at n.
claims.search_method: Direct induction along the ordered spine and leaf-edge traversal.

claims.evidence: The preceding construction gives distinct rank sums for every caterpillar, and claim 0 converts these orders into a graceful labeling. The one- and two-vertex cases are immediate.
claims.search_method: Deduction from the verified rank-sum construction and criterion.

claims.claim: Extreme-vertex leaf-extension lemma: if a graceful n-vertex tree has a vertex v labeled 1, attaching any s≥0 new leaves at v preserves gracefulness.
claims.evidence: Retain labels 1,...,n and label the new leaves n+1,...,n+s. Old differences are exactly 1,...,n−1, while the new edges incident with label 1 have differences n,...,n+s−1. These disjoint ranges give every required difference exactly once.

claims.claim: For every r≥0, the tree obtained from the once-subdivided K1,3 by adjoining r additional leaves to its center is a graceful non-caterpillar.
claims.evidence: For the seven-vertex subdivided claw, c=1 and (u_i,w_i)=(7,3),(6,5),(4,2) give differences 1,...,6. Labels 8,...,7+r on new center-leaves add differences 7,...,6+r. After deleting all leaves, the remaining vertices c,u1,u2,u3 induce K1,3, not a path, so every member is non-caterpillar.
claims.search_method: Direct all-r labeling formula and structural verification.
claims.witness: For each r, use edges c-u_i-u_i-w_i, the stated seven labels, and labels 8,...,7+r on the added center-leaves.

claims.claim: Any counterexample to the graceful tree conjecture must have at least 16 vertices and contain a vertex adjacent to at least three non-leaf vertices.
claims.evidence: Claim 10 excludes orders at most 15, and claim 2 excludes caterpillars. In a tree of relevant order, the non-leaves induce a connected subtree. If every vertex had at most two non-leaf neighbors, that induced subtree would have maximum degree at most two and hence be a path, making the original tree a caterpillar. Contraposition proves the asserted local structure.
claims.search_method: Deduction from the finite certification, caterpillar theorem, and a structural contrapositive.
